params.label: The cover's opening line; {product} = this edition's name

params.name: steps

default.title: Projects & portal
default.say: This screen is for documenting an application. You point {product} at a project, scan it for screens, and How to Use and the manuals build on that list.

default.title: Getting started
default.say: The Getting started list shows what is done and what is left: the portal's address, a project, its screens and email. Finished rows go quiet, so the next step is always clear.

default.title: Register a project
default.say: Press Register a project and give it a name and where its code lives: a folder on the server or a Git repository. Edit and Delete sit beside every project in the table.

default.title: Scan for screens
default.say: Scan for screens reads the project and lists every file that looks like a screen a person uses, in any framework. Add one by hand covers anything the scan misses.

default.title: Keep what is real
default.say: Tick the screens that are real, rename labels that read badly, and remove the rest. Save screens makes this the list every module works from; a later scan adds, never overwrites.

default.title: Narration
default.say: Set the How to get a Gemini key video and the Say-as list, one written = spoken pair per line. The narrator reads that list first, so your product's names are spoken properly.

default.title: Wire it into your app
default.say: Two framework-free ways to show your training inside your own product: fetch the links and draw your own button, or drop in the script the portal ships. Either way, help sits beside every screen.

params.label: The steps in order: title, say (the narration), target (where the spotlight goes; alternatives split by |, the first on screen wins), art (the picture: hero/flow/roads/meter/stack/check), place (below/above/right/left/center, optional), open (optional: what the guide presses first when the part is not on screen - open the first item, go back Home; alternatives split by |)
